description:
Recommends version upgrades for a package.json: the newest versions that are old enough and within the allowed step size, kept aligned with each other (peer dependencies and the first-level dependencies of the packages). Deterministic, no AI. Returns the new package.json, a unified diff (apply with `patch -p1`) and a per-package table with the reasons. Every package has an `explanation` sentence and `notes` lists other changes to the file (the `ripedeps` entry): relay them to the user as the rationale for each change.

Send the file as `packageJson` (text) or as `packageJsonUrl` (https URL of a raw file), exactly one of them.

Recommended: minAgeDays 7 (versions younger than 7 days are not proposed). The default is 0, or the `ripedeps` entry of the file. maxBump defaults to minor. Use `focus` to restrict the upgrade to some packages (and their direct neighbours).

Try more than one level: a plan only suggests and writes nothing, so calling again is cheap. Start with minor; if a package is held with a `level-limit` reason (a newer major exists), call again with maxBump "major" (optionally with `focus`) and compare. A `held` result is a reasoned decision for that one package, not a ban on the level: its reason names what blocks it (a peer or dependency constraint). Apply a larger step only when the user approves it.

Privacy: We do not keep your package.json: every upload is processed from scratch and discarded, nothing about its content or your IP address is remembered. Only anonymous statistics (file size, number of dependencies, number of changes) are counted.

focus.description: Exact names or * globs; a bare name like "trpc" also matches @trpc/*. Empty means global

maxBump.description: Default minor, or the ripedeps entry of the file

minAgeDays.description: Minimum age of a version since its release (default 0, or the ripedeps entry of the file)

packageJson.description: The full text of package.json (formatting is preserved in the diff)

packageJsonUrl.description: https URL of a package.json that the service downloads (use the raw file URL)

skipAdoptConfig.description: Do not write the effective settings into the output package.json

name: plan_upgrade

exact.description: false when the solver budget was exhausted and the best solution found is returned

value.description: Highest allowed step relative to the version in package.json

stale.description: true when expired package metadata was served because revalidation failed

notes.description: Changes to the output file that are not package upgrades (e.g. the ripedeps entry)

explanation.description: One sentence saying what happened to this package and why

publishedAt.description: Release time of the new version (ISO 8601)

title: Plan package.json upgrades
